newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine revises 96 grain harvest down, wheat up.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine revises 96 grain harvest down, wheat up.

text.p: Ukraine's 1996 grain harvest is a net 25.4 million tonnes, well below 1995's 36.5 million tonnes and below earlier estimates of 26.0 million, the deputy prime minister in charge of agriculture said in a statement on Friday.

Mykhailo Zubets' statement said that Ukraine harvested only 13.4 million tonnes of winter wheat last year, down from 16.4 million tonnes in 1995 but slightly above previous estimates of around 13.0 million.
Official data showed the crop results to be the poorest for the country since 1960.
President Leonid Kuchma told a meeting with government representatives on Friday that the country needed to restore its position on the world grain market.
"We need to revive our usual grain harvests within two or three years," Kuchma said, referring to the Soviet era when Ukraine's harvests were 40-50 million tonnes a year.
The government blamed drought at the beginning of the growing season as well as a lack of fertilisers, equipment and fuel for the sharp falls.
Last summer it forecast 1996 output at 36 million tonnes.
Ukraine needs about 10 million tonnes of grain for domestic consumption.
Officials said last year that Ukraine could export up to three million tonnes of winter wheat from the 1996 harvest.

Zubets also said the government wanted to raise the 1997 grain harvest to 38 million tonnes and that farmers planned to use more fertilisers to improve crop yields. --Yuri Kulikov, Kiev newsroom, +380 44 229 2264
